current_round.prompt: When the focus is in the terminal or agent toolbar area, keyboard shortcuts like Ctrl+k (to delete line) should function as expected instead of being captured by the browser to launch the typeahead menu. One solution is to use a different keyboard shortcut, such as Ctrl+p, but in general the terminal should support bash movement/editing shortcuts when the focus is on the terminal or agent tabs.

findings.description: The checklist changes a document-level capture listener without requiring regression coverage, so an implementation could still consume Ctrl/Cmd+K from a nested xterm focus target or accidentally disable the palette outside the toolbar.
findings.recommendation: Add focused DOM tests proving a nested toolbar key target is not prevented, stopped, or palette-opening, while an outside target still opens the palette and existing modal behavior remains unchanged.

result.summary: Add focused regression coverage proving Ctrl/Cmd+K yields inside the toolbar and still opens the palette elsewhere.

checklist.description: Change command-palette shortcut handling to ignore Ctrl/Cmd+K events from the toolbar dock or any descendant before preventing the event, stopping propagation, or opening the palette, while preserving the existing non-palette modal guard.

Add focused command-palette DOM regression coverage showing that Ctrl/Cmd+K from a nested toolbar target remains unconsumed and does not open the palette, an outside target still opens the palette and consumes the shortcut, and an existing non-palette modal still suppresses the palette.
Update the command-palette browser intent page to state that global palette shortcuts yield to focused toolbar terminal interactions.

criticism_resolutions.resolution: P2 requires nested-toolbar, outside-target, and existing-modal DOM regressions that cover both sides of the document-level capture boundary.

result.summary: The command palette's global Ctrl/Cmd+K handler will yield whenever keyboard focus is within the toolbar dock so terminal and agent tabs receive native shell and TUI editing shortcuts, while the palette shortcut remains available elsewhere and the documented browser shortcut contract reflects that precedence.

checklist.evidence: Updated src/surfaces/web/static/js/command-palette.js so the document-capture Ctrl/Cmd+K handler returns when #toolbar-dock contains the event target, before preventDefault, stopPropagation, or palette opening; the existing non-palette modal guard remains intact.

Added command-palette DOM regressions proving nested toolbar Ctrl+K and Cmd+K remain unconsumed and do not open the palette, an outside target is consumed and opens it, and an existing non-palette modal still suppresses it.
Updated docs/intent/04-surfaces/03-browser/03-command-palette.md to state that global palette shortcuts yield to focused toolbar terminal and agent interactions.
